Context: This excerpt is from a document that served as the constitution of Pennsylvania from `text(1701)` to `text(1776)`.
Title: Source 5: [Adapted from] the Charter of Privileges (1701)
Content: I, William Penn, Proprietor and Governor of Pennsylvania, grant unto all freemen, farmers, and residents of this colony these liberties and rights.

An assembly for the governing of Pennsylvania shall be chosen `text(each year)` by the freemen of the colony. This assembly shall consist of `text(four)` persons out of `text(each county)`. Assembly members should be those of most notable virtue, wisdom, and ability. This assembly shall have the power to choose their officers. They shall decide on the qualifications and elections of their own members. They shall appoint committees. They shall prepare bills in order to pass into laws. And they shall have all other powers and privileges of an assembly.

The laws of this government shall be made in this style: by the governor, with the consent of the freemen in the General Assembly; and after shall be confirmed by the governor and recorded and kept at Philadelphia.
